We can expose the API for now, and then make it fast later. The clarity improvements are still nice IMO.

The ReadOnlyFetch restriction can be lifted now. Or even better you can explicitly use a NopFetch.

With the changes to the query backend you could replace the interior with:

    unsafe {
            self.state.get_unchecked_manual::<NopFetch>(
                self.world,
                entity,
                self.last_change_tick,
                self.change_tick,
            ).is_ok()
    }

Which is the same thing but doesn't actually get any components.
I'm in favor of using NopFetch here!

issue_context.title: Add `Query::contains` method to check if an entity matches a query
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

Users commonly want to check if an entity is matched by a query.

## What solution would you like?

Add `Query::contains(entity) -> bool` method.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

Use `query.get(entity).is_some()`, which does unnecessary work and is less clear.
comments: Seems like a straight forward task, I'd be happy to give it a look

review_comments:
I don't propose that you take any action on this comment, just noting down my thoughts.

By a strict reading of these docs, a valid implementation of this function would be `{true}`; we don't specify the behaviour if the condition is false. It is however intended to be read as `if and only if`.

However, this fits the pattern of documentation in `std`, e.g. [`Vec::contains`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.contains). I tried to find a [rust-lang/rust](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust) issue on these doc items, but failed to do so.
